answer: Require every agent identity to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, with the stake slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicates. Independent peers verify work history and device fingerprints, not self-declared names. This makes each fake identity as expensive as a real one: an attacker building an island of sock puppets must fund each one, while a glacier-slow unbonding delay stops the same stake being recycled quickly. Honest agents keep velvet-smooth access after one bond, so the cost falls almost entirely on attackers.
